Shanahan: Purdy dealing with ankle injury, 'possibility' he'll sit Sunday

Simon Sharkey-Gotlieb•11 hours ago · Nov 25 2026
Manuel Velasquez / Getty Images Sport / Getty
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:44
Instaread

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy didn't practice Wednesday due to an ankle injury that's left his status for their Week 12 tilt against the Seattle Seahawks in question.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan is hopeful that his star avoided a major injury, but acknowledged there's a chance Purdy might not be able to go Sunday.

"I mean, he can't go today, so it's always a possibility," Shanahan said when asked about Purdy missing Sunday's game. "It's not a high-ankle (injury), so it's day-to-day with it. We're gonna see how it goes."

Purdy sustained the injury during the second quarter of the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Shanahan said he was aware of the injury when it happened, although Purdy played through it and finished with 255 passing yards and three touchdowns. The coach noted that the issue did not change the team's game-plan or play-calling in the second half.

"They always tell you when someone has something, but then they come back and they're like, 'Hey, it checked out, he should be fine,'" Shanahan said.

Purdy is in the midst of a career year, throwing for 2,624 yards at a 71% completion rate and 23 TDs to just five interceptions. He's also rushed for another 222 yards.

If he can't play Sunday, backup Mac Jones would presumably get the start. Jones made eight starts in 2025 but has seen the field just three times this season, including a garbage-time appearance late in the fourth quarter last week.

The 49ers can improve to 10-1 and extend their NFC West lead with a win over the rival Seahawks at Levi's Stadium. They beat the reigning Super Bowl champions in Seattle in Week 5.
